title: Rational and Irrational Numbers Core Test
description: Classify real numbers, analyze decimal patterns, simplify radicals, and explain rational and irrational reasoning.

questions.questionText: Why is -12 a rational number?
options: It can be written as -12/1
It is negative
It has no decimal point
Every negative number is irrational
questions.explanation: An integer is rational because it can be written as the integer divided by 1.

questions.questionText: Which number is rational because it is already written as a ratio of integers?
options: π
questions.explanation: The fraction 7/11 is a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator.

questions.questionText: Classify 0.375.
options: Irrational, because it has three decimal places
Irrational, because it is less than 1
Rational, because the decimal terminates
Not a real number
questions.explanation: A terminating decimal can be written over a power of ten: 0.375 = 375/1000 = 3/8.

questions.questionText: Classify 0.272727..., where the block 27 repeats forever.
options: Irrational, because the decimal never ends
Irrational, because 27 is not a perfect square
Not a real number
Rational, because the decimal repeats
questions.explanation: Every repeating decimal can be converted to a fraction, so it is rational.

questions.questionText: Which number is irrational?
options: π
questions.explanation: The exact value π has a nonterminating, nonrepeating decimal. The other choices are rational approximations or integers.

questions.questionText: Classify √49.
options: Irrational, because every square root is irrational
Rational, because √49 = 7
Irrational, because 49 is odd
Not a real number
questions.explanation: Since 49 is a perfect square, √49 equals the rational integer 7.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly classifies √7?
options: It is rational because 7 is an integer
It is rational because every radical is a fraction
It is irrational because 7 is not a perfect square
It is not real because 7 is positive
questions.correctAnswer: It is irrational because 7 is not a perfect square
questions.explanation: The square root of a positive integer that is not a perfect square is irrational.

questions.questionText: Classify -√81.
options: Irrational, because the value is negative
Irrational, because it contains a radical
Not real, because square roots cannot be negative
Rational, because -√81 = -9
questions.explanation: The radical simplifies first: √81 = 9, so -√81 = -9, which is rational.

questions.questionText: Which fraction shows that 0 is rational?
questions.explanation: Zero can be written as 0 divided by any nonzero integer. A denominator cannot be zero.

questions.questionText: The decimal 0.101001000100001... has groups of zeros that keep getting longer. How should it be classified?
options: Rational, because it contains only 0s and 1s
Irrational, because it does not terminate or repeat a fixed block
Rational, because the first digits show a pattern
Irrational, because every decimal is irrational
questions.correctAnswer: Irrational, because it does not terminate or repeat a fixed block
questions.explanation: A visible rule is not the same as a repeating block. The decimal continues without a fixed repeating block.

questions.questionText: Which list contains only irrational numbers?
questions.explanation: Both 2 and 11 are non-perfect squares, and π is irrational. Every other list includes a rational number.

questions.questionText: Which list contains only rational numbers?
questions.explanation: -5 is an integer, 0.125 terminates, and √100 = 10. All three are rational.

questions.questionText: A student claims, “Any number written with a square-root symbol is irrational.” Which example disproves the claim?
options: √6 is between 2 and 3
√10 does not terminate
√15 is not an integer
questions.explanation: One counterexample is enough to disprove the claim. √64 simplifies to the rational integer 8.

questions.questionText: How do the numbers 3.14159 and π differ?
options: Both are irrational because their digits begin the same way
3.14159 is rational, while π is irrational
3.14159 is irrational, while π is rational
Both are rational because 3.14159 approximates π
questions.correctAnswer: 3.14159 is rational, while π is irrational
questions.explanation: The terminating decimal 3.14159 is a rational approximation. The exact value π is irrational.

questions.questionText: Which is the best classification of √121?
options: A rational non-integer
An irrational number
A rational integer
A non-real number
questions.explanation: √121 = 11, so its most specific classification among the choices is a rational integer.

questions.questionText: Why is √50 irrational?
options: 50 is even, and square roots of even numbers are always irrational
50 is greater than 10
The symbol √ always produces an irrational value
50 is not a perfect square, so √50 cannot be written as a ratio of integers
questions.correctAnswer: 50 is not a perfect square, so √50 cannot be written as a ratio of integers
questions.explanation: A positive integer has a rational square root only when it is a perfect square.

questions.questionText: Classify √36 + 1/2.
options: Rational, because it equals 13/2
Irrational, because it contains a square root
Irrational, because it is not an integer
Not real, because a radical cannot be added to a fraction
questions.explanation: √36 + 1/2 = 6 + 1/2 = 13/2, a ratio of integers.

questions.questionText: Classify 3 + √2.
options: Rational, because 3 is rational
Irrational, because adding rational 3 does not remove the irrational part √2
Rational, because every sum is rational
Not real, because unlike number types cannot be added
questions.correctAnswer: Irrational, because adding rational 3 does not remove the irrational part √2
questions.explanation: The sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.

questions.questionText: Which fraction is equal to 0.125 and confirms that it is rational?
questions.explanation: 0.125 = 125/1000, which simplifies to 1/8.

questions.questionText: The decimal 0.454545... repeats the block 45. Which conclusion is correct?
options: It is irrational because it has infinitely many digits
It is irrational because 45 is not a perfect square
It is rational only if the digits eventually stop
It is rational because a repeating decimal can be converted to a fraction
questions.correctAnswer: It is rational because a repeating decimal can be converted to a fraction
questions.explanation: Repeating decimals have exact fractional representations even though their digits continue forever.

questions.questionText: Which decimal is irrational?
questions.explanation: The number of zeros keeps changing, so there is no fixed repeating block. The other decimals terminate or repeat.

questions.questionText: Which expression proves that the mixed number -2 3/5 is rational?
questions.explanation: -2 3/5 equals -(10/5 + 3/5) = -13/5, a ratio of integers.

questions.questionText: A circle has diameter 1 meter. Its exact circumference is π meters. Which statement is true?
options: The exact circumference is the rational number 3.14
The exact circumference terminates after enough digits
The exact circumference is irrational
The circumference is not a real number
questions.explanation: With diameter 1, C = πd = π. The exact value π is irrational; 3.14 is only an approximation.

questions.questionText: A square has area 144 square centimeters. How should its side length be classified?
options: Irrational, because all side lengths from areas use radicals
Irrational, because 144 has three digits
Not real, because area cannot determine side length
Rational, because √144 = 12
questions.explanation: The side length is √144 = 12 centimeters, a rational integer.

questions.questionText: A square has area 72 square meters. Which classification describes its exact side length √72?
options: Irrational, because 72 is not a perfect square
Rational, because 72 is an integer
Rational, because all measurements are rational
Not real, because 72 is not a perfect square
questions.correctAnswer: Irrational, because 72 is not a perfect square
questions.explanation: The exact side length is real, but it is irrational because 72 is not a perfect square.

questions.questionText: Classify √81 / 3.
options: Irrational, because it contains a radical
Rational, because it equals 3
Irrational, because division creates irrational numbers
Not real, because radicals cannot be divided
questions.explanation: Simplify first: √81 / 3 = 9/3 = 3.

questions.questionText: Classify 2√5.
options: Rational, because it is a product of 2 and 5
Rational, because multiplying by 2 removes the radical
Irrational, because a nonzero rational multiple of √5 remains irrational
Not real, because √5 is not an integer
questions.correctAnswer: Irrational, because a nonzero rational multiple of √5 remains irrational
questions.explanation: √5 is irrational, and multiplying it by nonzero rational 2 does not make it rational.

questions.questionText: Simplify and classify √18 / √2.
options: Irrational, because both original radicals are irrational
Irrational, because it equals √16
Not real, because radicals cannot be divided
Rational, because it equals √9 = 3
questions.explanation: For positive values, √18 / √2 = √(18/2) = √9 = 3, which is rational.

questions.questionText: Simplify and classify √8 × √2.
options: Rational, because it equals √16 = 4
Irrational, because each factor is irrational
Rational, because it equals 10
Not real, because radicals cannot be multiplied
questions.explanation: √8 × √2 = √16 = 4. Two irrational factors can have a rational product.

questions.questionText: How should -π be classified?
options: Rational, because every negative number is rational
Irrational, because changing the sign does not create a fractional representation
Rational, because -π is less than zero
Not real, because π cannot be negative
questions.correctAnswer: Irrational, because changing the sign does not create a fractional representation
questions.explanation: The opposite of an irrational number is still irrational.

questions.questionText: The decimal 0.999... repeats forever. Which statement is correct?
options: It is irrational because it never terminates
It is rational but can never equal a fraction
It is rational and equals 1
It is less than every rational number
questions.explanation: The repeating decimal 0.999... is exactly equal to 1, so it is rational.

questions.questionText: Let x = 0.666.... Which equation is the useful first step for converting x to a fraction?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 10 shifts one repeating digit so subtracting x will eliminate the repeating part.

questions.questionText: What must be true about the decimal representation of any rational number?
options: It terminates or eventually repeats
It always terminates
It never contains a repeating digit
It must have fewer than ten decimal places
questions.explanation: A rational number's decimal expansion either ends or eventually repeats a fixed block.

questions.questionText: Which description defines an irrational number?
options: A negative number that cannot be shown on a number line
A real number that cannot be written as a ratio of two integers
A decimal with more than three digits
A number written using a square-root symbol
questions.correctAnswer: A real number that cannot be written as a ratio of two integers
questions.explanation: The defining feature is the impossibility of writing the exact value as a/b for integers a and nonzero b.

questions.questionText: Classify √0.
options: Irrational, because it contains a radical
Not real, because zero has no square root
Rational, because √0 = 0
Irrational, because zero is neither positive nor negative
questions.explanation: Since 0 × 0 = 0, √0 = 0, and zero is rational.

questions.questionText: Which statement is always true?
options: Every rational number is an integer
Every square root is irrational
Every nonterminating decimal is irrational
Every integer is rational
questions.explanation: Every integer n can be written as n/1. Rational numbers also include fractions, and repeating nonterminating decimals are rational.

questions.questionText: Simplify and classify √(16/25).
options: Rational, because it equals 4/5
Irrational, because it contains a fraction under a radical
Rational, because it equals 16/25
Not real, because square roots cannot contain fractions
questions.explanation: √(16/25) = √16/√25 = 4/5, which is rational.

questions.questionText: Simplify and classify √0.04.
options: Irrational, because 0.04 is a decimal
Rational, because it equals 0.2
Irrational, because it equals 0.02
Not real, because square roots require whole numbers
questions.explanation: Since 0.2 × 0.2 = 0.04, √0.04 = 0.2, a terminating rational decimal.

questions.questionText: Which reasoning correctly classifies √0.2?
options: It is rational because 0.2 terminates
It is rational because every number less than 1 is rational
It is irrational because √0.2 = √(1/5), and 1/5 is not the square of a rational number
It is not real because 0.2 is not an integer
questions.correctAnswer: It is irrational because √0.2 = √(1/5), and 1/5 is not the square of a rational number
questions.explanation: A rational number can have an irrational square root. The terminating input 0.2 does not make its square root rational.

questions.questionText: Simplify and classify π - π.
options: Irrational, because both terms are irrational
Irrational, because π cannot be canceled
Not real, because irrational numbers cannot be subtracted
Rational, because it equals 0
questions.explanation: π - π = 0. Two irrational numbers can have a rational difference.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly classifies π + 1?
options: It is irrational because adding rational 1 to π cannot produce a rational sum
It is rational because 1 is rational
It is rational because π is close to 3
It is not real because unlike number types cannot be added
questions.correctAnswer: It is irrational because adding rational 1 to π cannot produce a rational sum
questions.explanation: If π + 1 were rational, subtracting rational 1 would make π rational, which is impossible.

questions.questionText: Simplify and classify (√5)².
options: Irrational, because √5 is irrational
Rational, because it equals 5
Rational, because it equals 25
Not real, because an irrational number cannot be squared
questions.explanation: Squaring √5 reverses the square root, producing the rational integer 5.

questions.questionText: Simplify and classify √48 / √3.
options: Irrational, because 48 and 3 are not perfect squares
Irrational, because it equals √45
Rational, because it equals √16 = 4
Not real, because radicals cannot form a quotient

questions.questionText: Which irrational number lies between 4 and 5?
questions.explanation: Since 16 < 20 < 25, 4 < √20 < 5. Because 20 is not a perfect square, √20 is irrational.

questions.questionText: Which choice is a rational approximation of the irrational number π?
options: 2π
questions.explanation: 22/7 is a fraction and therefore rational. It is close to π but is not exactly equal to π.

questions.questionText: Which relationship among number sets is correct?
options: Every rational number is an integer, and every integer is irrational
Every integer is rational, and every rational number is real
Every real number is rational
Rational and irrational numbers are not real numbers
questions.correctAnswer: Every integer is rational, and every rational number is real
questions.explanation: Integers are contained within the rational numbers, and rational numbers are contained within the real numbers.

questions.questionText: A student says, “The sum of two irrational numbers is always irrational.” Which counterexample disproves the statement?
questions.explanation: Both √2 and -√2 are irrational, but their sum is rational zero.

questions.questionText: A student says, “The product of two irrational numbers is always irrational.” Which counterexample disproves the statement?
questions.explanation: Both factors are irrational, but their product is the rational integer 2.

questions.questionText: Which decimal has a fixed repeating block and is therefore rational?
questions.explanation: The block 1234 repeats unchanged. The other choices follow changing patterns rather than one fixed repeating block.

questions.questionText: A 3-by-4 rectangle has a diagonal of √(3² + 4²) units. How should the diagonal be classified?
options: Irrational, because every diagonal is irrational
Rational, because √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5
Irrational, because it is found with a square root
Not real, because 3² + 4² is greater than either side
questions.explanation: The exact diagonal simplifies to √25 = 5. Its geometric origin does not determine its number type.
